items.title: Anthropic donates Agent Skills, its open agent-standard, to the Agentic AI Foundation
items.summary: Anthropic handed the Agent Skills standard — name, logo, GitHub org, and the agentskills.io domain — to the Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF), which it co-founded with Block and OpenAI and which already holds Anthropic's donated Model Context Protocol. Since the standard launched in December 2025, 70+ platforms (ChatGPT, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, VS Code) have adopted it, with nearly 1M skills published and ~280M installs.
items.whyItMatters: Agent Skills' pattern of packaged, versioned knowledge/workflow modules is a reusable model for giving Romain or Anna specialized tutoring behaviors (grammar drills, exam prep, pronunciation feedback) without bespoke prompt engineering or retraining.

items.title: China reportedly clears DeepSeek and MiniMax for overseas AI model use
items.summary: A CCTV-affiliated social account (Yuyuan Tantian) said on Oct 22 that DeepSeek and MiniMax have won approval for global/overseas use of their AI models, under Beijing's draft AI export-control rules (proposed Oct 16) covering 23 AI technologies; licensing for open-source exports is reportedly simplified, though API/SaaS sales stay outside the approval. Neither company has confirmed it, and this surfaced two days after the US ordered federal agencies to strip DeepSeek from their systems.
items.whyItMatters: Easier overseas distribution of cheap Chinese open-weight models could keep downward pressure on LLM backend costs for the tutor's reasoning layer, though US compliance restrictions complicate actually adopting DeepSeek in production.
